summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and recurrent febrile episodes was admitted for evaluation of fever, chills, and myalgias recurring every six weeks. He also reported new-onset dysuria and urinary urgency. Initial workup showed mild leukocytosis, normal renal and liver function, and negative urine and blood cultures. Imaging revealed mild intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation raising a radiographic concern for cholangitis, but clinically this was deemed unlikely due to absence of fever, normal labs, and negative cultures. CT chest showed nonspecific ground-glass opacities, likely chronic, with no respiratory symptoms. CMV viral load was negative. The patient remained afebrile throughout admission and improved symptomatically. He was discharged home on his baseline immunosuppressive and prophylactic medications with plans for close follow-up in the liver clinic and outpatient echocardiography to evaluate a new holosystolic murmur.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of prostate
